Transfer GPU table data back to R

Source: R/collect.R
collect.tbl_gpu.Rd

Copies data from GPU memory back to R as a tibble. This is typically the final step in a GPU data manipulation pipeline, after filtering, mutating, and selecting the data you need.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
collect(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Additional arguments (ignored, included for compatibility).

Value

A tibble::tibble containing the data from the GPU table (a grouped_df, with the same .drop, when x is grouped, as for dplyr::collect() on a database table). A table uploaded from a plain data.frame comes back as a bare data.frame while it is ungrouped, and custom data-frame attributes (attr(df, "foo")) are kept the way dplyr keeps them through verbs. Column types are converted back to R types:

  • FLOAT64/FLOAT32 -> numeric (double)

  • INT8/INT16/INT32, UINT8/UINT16 -> integer

  • UINT32 -> double (exact)

  • INT64/UINT64 -> bit64::integer64 (a double with a warning when bit64 is absent and a value is past 2^53); a UINT64 value past INT64_MAX is an error, never a wrap

  • STRING -> character

  • BOOL8 -> logical (TRUE/FALSE)

  • DATE (TIMESTAMP_DAYS) -> Date; TIMESTAMP_SECONDS/MILLISECONDS/ MICROSECONDS/NANOSECONDS -> POSIXct (nanoseconds finer than a microsecond are rounded, with a warning)

  • DURATION_DAYS -> difftime in days; the other DURATION_* -> difftime in seconds (a warning past 2^53 ticks)

  • DECIMAL32/64/128 -> double, the nearest one (a warning when it needs more than 15 significant digits; an error beyond the double range)

  • a dictionary with string keys -> factor

Any other type (LIST, STRUCT, a dictionary with other keys) is an error of class cuplyr_error_unsupported_gpu_type naming the column; the warnings have class cuplyr_warning_collect_precision and name every column concerned. print() and glimpse() show such a column as a placeholder.

Details

Grouped tables and .drop

The .drop setting of group_by() travels with the table through the verbs that keep at least one group column (and is reset to the default when none is left; group_by() on a grouped table keeps it unless given a new .drop), so group_by(f, .drop = FALSE) |> arrange(x) |> collect() still keeps empty factor-level groups. Empty groups of a non-factor column that filter() or slice() emptied are not kept, unlike in dplyr, except after slice(.preserve = TRUE), which keeps its input's group keys: see the .drop section of group_by().

Memory considerations

Collecting transfers all data from GPU to CPU memory. For large datasets, this can be slow and memory-intensive. Best practice is to:

  1. Filter rows to reduce data volume

  2. Select only needed columns

  3. Then collect the results

Performance

Data transfer between GPU and CPU is limited by PCIe bandwidth (typically 16-32 GB/s). For a 1 GB dataset, expect ~50-100ms transfer time.

See also

tbl_gpu for creating GPU tables, filter.tbl_gpu, select.tbl_gpu for reducing data

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)

  # Process on GPU, then collect
  result <- gpu_mtcars |>
    filter(mpg > 20) |>
    mutate(kpl = mpg * 0.425) |>
    select(mpg, kpl, hp) |>
    collect()

  # Result is a regular tibble
  class(result)
  print(result)
}
